articles.title: The best gadget I bought this year is a milk frother
articles.summary: I bought a milk frother and I’ve been making fancy coffee drinks ever since.
articles.body: Back in February, I went to Los Angeles to take in some art and stayed in Koreatown. Down the street from my hotel, there was this little coffee shop — Stagger — that is, I think, best known for its matcha, which is good. But the drink I unexpectedly found myself obsessed with was their cream top, an iced Americano with, yep, vanilla cream on top. When I got back to Oakland, I kept thinking about how badly I wanted one. For more than 20 years, I’ve been drinking my coffee — iced or otherwise — black. Originally this was because I knew I could put black coffee that had cooled off in the microwave to reheat it without worrying that the milk in it would curdle. (Gross, I know.) Then, as I started drinking better coffee, it felt like the best way to appreciate the expensive beans I was buying. So my attachment to the cream top surprised me. And then, when Oakland had a gnarly heat wave in March, I decided there was one way I’d tolerate it: fancy coffee drinks. I splashed out $14 for the Zulay Kitchen frother and I was off. A handheld foamer looks and works kinda like an immersion blender. I pour milk into a glass, stick the frother in there, and then hold the power button until it reaches my preferred consistency. When the disposable batteries it uses are fresh, this takes about 30 seconds to a minute. As the batteries degrade, it takes longer; if I’m getting impatient about how long it’s taking me to make my frothy treats, it’s time to change the batteries. The frother also works to beat eggs, mix protein powder or creatine into a drink, and make hot chocolate. But by far it’s gotten the most use making my coffee drinks as I set out to make a cream top of my own. [Image: Also I think it’s neat to watch the foam descend into the coffee. The cream top descended from the Einspänner, an espresso drink that’s named for a one-horse carriage. The original Viennese version used hot espresso, and the whipped cream on top served as a kind of insulation, which kept the drivers’ drinks hot for them when they were out in the cold. (Obviously, its popularity expanded beyond carriage drivers.) It isn’t clear to me how the Einspänner made it to South Korea, but it exploded in popularity there, with all kinds of variations, mostly iced. And then from South Korea, it made its way to the US, where the ground had already been cleared by Starbucks’ “cold foam” drinks. The notable thing about the cream top, besides the addition of delicious fat and sugar to coffee, was that the cream wasn’t as light as latte foam, but wasn’t as heavy as ordinary whipped cream. It was melty and dripped slowly into the coffee. My first experiments with my at-home cream top were pretty simple. I don’t have an espresso machine, but I do make concentrated cold brew in hot weather, which has a strong enough flavor to stand up against the foam. (Some recipes suggest powdered espresso if you don’t want to use concentrated cold brew.) After I mastered the simple cream top, I began making forays into weirder breakfast treats, my favorite of which I… recreated from a Starbucks ad. It’s a cold brew with coconut ube cold foam, the top of which I dust with toasted coconut flakes. It is dank. (This is a recipe for a more sophisticated version than I make.) So when it was 90 degrees in Oakland for about two weeks running recently, this drink was how I consoled myself. To be honest, I’m just recommending getting a frother. You can spend a lot on a milk frother and some people do. I relied on America’s Test Kitchen to steer me in the right direction — but outlets like Wirecutter and Bon Appétit have their own preferred options. This one is cheap and simple, and it’s been treating me right. I’m sure the Apple HomeView is nice, too, but in pleasure per dollar can it match a $14 cold foamer that takes AA batteries? I have my doubts.

articles.body: Ashley St. Clair, a former conservative influencer and author, has found herself at the centre of renewed attention following explosive claims about her relationship with Elon Musk in the new documentary Musk. She alleges that the billionaire reduced her monthly child support payments after she refused to sign a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and publicly revealed that she had given birth to their son, Romulus, in 2024.According to St. Clair, she was offered $15 million upfront and $100,000 a month in child support in exchange for keeping their relationship private. She claims that after she rejected the proposal, the monthly payments were reduced from $100,000 to $40,000 and subsequently to $20,000 after she went public with the birth in February 2025. Musk has disputed her account of the alleged NDA offer.Who is Ashley St. Clair?St. Clair, 28, rose to prominence as a conservative social media personality, building a following on X through posts expressing right-wing views. She also worked with the satirical website The Babylon Bee and made appearances on Fox News.Beyond her online presence, St. Clair is an author. She wrote Elephants Are Not Birds, a children's book published by Brave Books and described as a Christian conservative work exploring identity.In January 2026, she indicated that she was reconsidering her political views and said she was removing her name as the book's author.How Ashley St. Clair met Elon MuskSt. Clair has said her interactions with Musk began in 2023, when he started responding to her posts on X, formerly Twitter. Their online exchanges eventually developed into a relationship that she described as emotionally intimate.Recalling one of their early interactions, St. Clair said Musk responded to a Mother's Day post by encouraging her to have more children. She also recalled him telling her that she should have 10 children and suggesting that they have a child together.St. Clair has said Musk presented himself as a devoted father and appeared to maintain amicable relationships with the mothers of his other children.She later became pregnant and gave birth to Romulus in 2024. She publicly disclosed the birth in February 2025, bringing their relationship into the public eye.Ashley St. Clair’s claims about the NDA and child supportIn Musk, St. Clair alleges that she was offered $15 million upfront and $100,000 in monthly payments if she signed an NDA preventing her from discussing their relationship.She says she rejected the proposal because she did not want her son to grow up feeling that he was a secret.St. Clair claims Musk subsequently reduced her monthly payments to $40,000 and then to $20,000 after she publicly revealed the child's birth.Musk has disputed her account of the alleged agreement, reportedly stating on X that she was never offered the deal on the terms she described and accusing her of making false claims.The two have also been involved in a custody dispute over Romulus. He also said he was “not against finding out” whether he was the child's father.What Ashley St. Clair has revealed about Musk’s desire to have childrenThe documentary also features St. Clair's account of Musk's desire to have a large family. She alleges that other women contacted her after interacting with the billionaire online and described conversations about having children with him.St. Clair also recalled an alleged text message in which Musk expressed a desire to have a “legion of children before the civil war”.Musk has publicly acknowledged having numerous children with different women. He most recently welcomed another child, Seldon Lycurgus, with Neuralink executive Shivon Zilis, according to reports cited in the documentary's coverage.Directed by Alex Gibney, Musk examines the billionaire's public image, private relationships and ambitions. articles.title: Jason Sudeikis Hopes to Continue ‘Ted Lasso’ for Season 5, Says Coverage of Split From Olivia Wilde Missed a ‘Million Little Things’: ‘It’s Always More Complicated’
articles.summary: Jason Sudeikis opened up on a recent episode of “Talk Easy with Sam Fragoso,” discussing his hopes for “Ted Lasso” Season 5, how the show “saved” him from “s...
articles.body:
Jason Sudeikis opened up on a recent episode of " Talk Easy with Sam Fragoso ," discussing his hopes for "Ted Lasso" Season 5, how the show "saved" him from "self-harm" and what the public got wrong about his closely followed 2020 split from ex Olivia Wilde.

Sudeikis and Fragoso talked "Ted Lasso" up top, as the host asked whether the actor wanted to continue the show for Seasons 5 and 6. (The Season 4 finale aired earlier this month.) Sudeikis said he "would like to," but the status of future seasons remains unknown: "Yeah, I just don't know," he said, assuring Fragoso he wasn't being coy "intentionally." "We haven't started a writers' room or anything like that," he noted. He added that he would "assume" Apple would continue the show if the main cast wanted to return.

The former "Saturday Night Live" star also got candid about what "Ted Lasso" saved him from, as he's mentioned on multiple occasions. "Some form of self-harm. Flat out," Sudeikis answered, describing a feeling that he hadn't felt since "the confusing teenage years." " That's probably the rawest, most, maybe embarrassing, but I don't think it's embarrassing… It does bubble up shame in me to think like, 'How dare you? How dare you have those kinds of thoughts,' you know?" The actor continued to describe wanting to be a drummer or a dancer as a teen to get out his emotions. "So how did ['Ted Lasso'] save me? To a certain degree, it helped [and] it carried me as sometimes the work has done in the past."

Sudeikis's ex-fiancé, Olivia Wilde, also came up, as the host asked about what the "Ted Lasso" star feels the public coverage of their separation missed. (Sudeikis specifically made headlines in 2022 when Wilde was served with child custody documents during her appearance at CinemaCon .)

"Oh, gosh. I mean, a million little things," he responded. "But, but what's interesting is that it allows you capacity for empathy for when others go through those. And you need not be as lucky as we are to get to do something that we love."

He continued: "I don't wish it on anyone because I don't think it really moves the needle. And to be clear, this isn't like, all evil is just misunderstood or something like that. I just mean these, interpersonal situations that then get portrayed as being these binary situations of right and wrong… It's always more complicated, more human than that."

Sudeikis praised Wilde's work: "Olivia loves what she does and is very, very good at and always has been. I'm thrilled for her." (The actress and director is in the middle of the Oscars conversation f or her work on "The Invite.")

articles.title: ‘The Simpsons’ Surprise: Apu Is Heard for the First Time in Nearly a Decade, as Sunil Malhotra Takes Over for Hank Azaria (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for the Oct. 18 episode of “The Simpsons,” “The Revengening,” which aired Sunday night on Fox. “The Simps...
articles.body:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for the Oct. 18 episode of "The Simpsons," "The Revengening," which aired Sunday night on Fox.

"The Simpsons" has pulled off its own October surprise: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon is back. The fan favorite character finally spoke again for the first time in nearly a decade on Sunday night's episode, "The Revengening." Variety has exclusively learned who is behind Apu's new voice: actor and voice-over vet Sunil Malhotra ("Grey's Anatomy," "The Legend of Korra").

Malhotra's hiring and the return of Apu — who has been seen, but not heard on "The Simpsons" since the October 2017 episode "The Serfsons" — was a closely guarded secret inside "The Simpsons" universe. Fox didn't share a screener for "The Revengening," and producers kept both the episode's table read and its subsequent production under tight protocols (including NDAs for all involved).

Also heard on Sunday's episode was the debut of Janina Gavankar ("The Morning Show") as Apu's wife, Manjula. And now that Apu is back and the Kwik-E-Mart has reopened, executive producer Matt Selman said both characters and the Nahasapeemapetilon family will once again be seen (and heard) on "The Simpsons" more often.

"We love this character, and wanted to bring him back in a smart, 'Simpsons'-y way that allowed him to evolve," Selman said. "We're excited by what Sunil has already brought to the role, and look forward to seeing more of Apu in the future."

Hank Azaria previously voiced Apu, a character that has been controversial over the years due to its stereotypical portrayal of a South Asian convenience store clerk. The issue of Apu was the centerpiece of the 2017 documentary "The Problem With Apu," in which comedian Hari Kondabolu discussed the impact the character has had on people of South Asian descent.

After that doc made waves — including in "The Simpsons" writers' room, where it was screened and discussed — Azaria announced that he would no longer voice Apu. "I apologize for my part in creating that and participating in that," Azaria said in 2021 on Dax Shepard's podcast "Armchair Expert." "Part of me feels like I need to go to every single Indian person in this country and personally apologize. And sometimes I do."

In the aftermath, Apu was shifted to the background on "The Simpsons," as producers decided how to handle the character going forward. For years, that meant Apu would still occasionally be seen in Springfield, but never heard.

Until now. The idea of bringing back Apu this way, as one of this year's Halloween-themed episodes, came from staffer Nick Dahan (who's the credited writer on "The Revengening") and co-executive producer Cesar Mazariegos. After hearing their pitch, Selman said he thought it was "a brilliant way" to bring Apu back and reference the entire situation.

Voice actor Malhotra said he took time to look into what it would mean to take over Apu and talked to the producers to make sure the character was more culturally appropriate.

"When my agent called me about a 'Simpsons' audition, I knew exactly what role it was for, and the idea actually made my stomach sink," he said. "But admittedly, part of me was also curious. It had been eight years since Apu had spoken on the show, and it got me thinking: Did the writers' room look different now? Could they bring him back in a way that acknowledged and apologized for past mistakes? Could I make the character my own, and reclaim him in some way? And could they achieve all of that in an unmistakably 'Simpsons' way that didn't disappoint fans?

"Whether the producers knew it or not, I was prepared to walk away," he continued. Malhotra said that he declined his very first "professional job offer 28 years ago" because it would have required him to play a stereotypical "Hindu guy," adding that playing such a caricature "to be the butt of the joke wasn't something I was willing to do, and I've turned down similar work multiple times since."

But as Malhotra got further down the road with "The Simpsons," he said, he began engaging with the producers about their plans for Apu before he would commit to the role, where he was promised that the return of Apu was being handled with the utmost care.

"My callback was the first of many times that no one at 'The Simpsons' let me down," he said. "I told casting that I'd only consider an offer if I could meet showrunner Matt Selman and co-executive producer Cesar Mazariegos, both of whom gladly did so. It was the beginning of a deeply collaborative experience that I hope is equally satisfying for longtime fans of 'The Simpsons' and for other South Asian kids who, like me, stopped watching at some point along the way."

In "The Revengening," a spooky lead-up to next week's "Treehouse of Horror XXXVII," a man in a "Daft Monk" Halloween costume (as in, a Daft Punk helmet and monastic robe — wordplay!) is accidentally killed over and over again by Springfield residents all over town. A year later, "Daft Monk" is still alive, and getting his revenge by taking out his would-be killers, one by one.

Eventually "Daft Monk" summons the townspeople to Springfield City Hall, where he takes his helmet off and reveals that he's actually Apu.

"I'd be lying if I didn't say that the sweetest part of all was unleashing that righteously rage-fueled "I AM APU!" — on behalf of so many of us — over and over in the studio until we got it just right," Malhotra said. "I really feel like we did and I can't wait for fans to see more Apu."

Apu then shares his backstory: After he was nearly killed dozens of times, he wound up on "The Island of Forgotten Garbage," where he's healed by "The Simpsons" quack Dr. Nick (who also has been seen sparingly in recent years). "All the junk Springfield gets rid of winds up here," he tells Apu, "like you … If you wound up here, it's for a reason, right, Leon?" (Out pops the character that Michael Jackson played in the Season 3 episode "Stark Raving Mad," which was pulled from "Simpsons" rotation in 2019 after the doc "Leaving Neverland" showcased more allegations against the late pop star.)

Says Apu before he reveals himself: "I am the man you left for dead. I am the one you pretended never existed!"

Then, unmasked, he tells the Springfield crowd: "It would have been so easy to bring me back. I immediately ran home to my family, but they were gone. Then I went to the Kwik-E-Mart, and was shocked to find it abandoned. As I wandered aimlessly through town, no one even noticed me. It was as if I was invisible. That was when I vowed to take my revenge on Springfield."

He's about to light City Hall on fire, but Marge Simpson pipes up — representing the Springfield citizens, but also clearly serving as a mouthpiece for the show's producers: "Apu, we're so sorry we left you for dead. Believe me, we wanted to do the right thing."

Bart adds: "But we were so scared, and just didn't know what to do."

Lenny also chimes in, in a nod to the debates inside "The Simpsons" writers' room: "If it's any consolation, we had so many internal conversations about it."

But, Carl finishes, "Ahh, they kind of just didn't go anywhere." (And for almost a decade, that's how "The Simpsons" never got around to bringing back Apu.)

Homer then offers to sacrifice himself to save the rest of the town, and offers this penance to Apu, while reminding viewers how important Apu has been to the makeup of Springfield: "I'm just doing what the old Apu would have done. The guy who loved this town and everyone in it. You were on our bowling teams, our barbershop quartets, our dad rock cover bands. We took you for granted. I took you for granted."

But before Apu can blow up the town, he wakes up. It turns out it was a nightmare; no one is dead. He's back in the Kwik E-Mart, and Manjula is there too. So is his No. 1 customer, Homer, who invites him to a Halloween party.

"What the heck? I'll do it," Apu says. "A Halloween party sounds kind of fun. Plus, I feel like I haven't seen everyone in ages. Oh, but I wish I had a costume."

But he actually does: There's a "Daft Monk" costume stashed under the cash register. So was it really a dream? And that's the end of the episode — but Apu is back!

This isn't the first time "The Simpsons" writers used their characters to allude to their indecisiveness on what to do with Apu. In the 2018 episode "No Good Read Goes Unpunished," Marge begins reading her favorite childhood novel to Lisa, but quickly realizes the old book was a lot more offensive and racist than she remembered. She tries to sanitize it, but "now it's as inoffensive as a Sunday in Cincinnati … what am I supposed to do?"

Lisa then looks at the audience, seemingly addressing "Simpsons" fans: "It's hard to say. Something that started decades ago and was applauded and inoffensive is now politically incorrect. What can you do?"

The scene pulls back to reveal a photo of Apu near Lisa's bed, and it's obvious they're no longer talking about a book, but their own show. With Marge also looking straight at viewers, the two suggest that "Some things will be dealt with at a later date … if at all." (It should be noted that Apu and his children also appeared in the episode, but did not speak.)

In June 2020, during the post-George Floyd reckoning on race, "The Simpsons" announced that moving forward, its characters of color would be voiced by culturally appropriate actors. Among the major changes, Alex Désert took over as Carl Carlson from Azaria, and Kevin Michael Richardson (who had already been a part of the series cast) became Dr. Julius Hibbert, which was previously Harry Shearer. Now, Apu, with Malhotra taking over, joins that list as well.

And for several years, the creative team promised that they would address Apu at some point. In 2021, series creator Matt Groening told USA Today that the producers were first seeing if they could make new Apu stories work. "I think the Apu stories are fantastic, and he's one of the most nuanced characters on a silly two-dimensional cartoon show," Groening said in the interview.

Early reactions on social media about the return of Apu has already been positive : "Apu is back thank you Simpsons," said one. Another : "The Simpsons reveals the new voice for Apu. Representation for Indian Americans. Well played Matt Groening and Dan Castellaneta, Hank Azaria, Nancy Cartwright, Harry Shearer, Julie Kavner and Yeardley Smith." Wrote a third: "Apu reveal is the greatest thing to happen on the Simpsons in a long time. I missed that genius character!"

Malhotra's recent voice credits include "The Legend of Vox Machina," "The Loud House," "Monster High," "The Casagrandes" and "Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi." He's also been heard on video games including "Mortal Kombat 1," "Avatar: The Last Airbender – Quest of Balance" and "Marvel's Avengers." In TV, besides "Grey's Anatomy," he's also appeared on "ER," "NCIS: New Orleans," "MacGyver" and "Maron."

articles.title: New iPhone spyware can steal passwords and photos
articles.summary: P7 DarkSword iPhone spyware can steal saved passwords, photos, Apple Notes and cryptocurrency wallet data by checking for commands every 15 seconds.
articles.body: Your iPhone probably holds more personal information than your wallet. Think about the passwords you've saved, the photos you never intended to share and the private notes you keep handy. Now, security researchers have uncovered a more aggressive version of spyware designed to get its hands on that information. The threat is called P7 DarkSword, and researchers at mobile security company iVerify discovered it while investigating an infected iPhone. According to their Oct. 8, 2026, report, the spyware can collect sensitive information and communicate with attackers who can issue additional commands remotely. That sounds alarming, and it should get your attention. However, the research does not establish that every iPhone is vulnerable. Here's what researchers discovered and how you can better protect your device. YOUR PHONE SAYS IT'S UPDATED. CHECK OTHER SETTINGS, TOO Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will share five practical ways to protect your trip and your wallet this holiday travel season. You'll learn how to secure your phone and personal information, find better travel deals, avoid common scams, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed. Join us Saturday, October 31, at 11 AM ET / 8 AM PT. Register free now at CyberGuyLive.com. What is P7 DarkSword iPhone spyware? P7 DarkSword is a newly identified variant of DarkSword, an existing iPhone spyware family. Researchers at iVerify discovered it while investigating a suspicious infection in August 2026. Their security system had flagged unusual activity on a customer's device. After examining the phone with the customer's permission, the team discovered that the spyware behaved differently from versions they had previously encountered. The researchers also searched for related malicious code using the Validin threat intelligence platform. Eventually, they identified another version of the spyware hosted on suspicious infrastructure. Their analysis revealed that the attackers had modified the code to make it more capable and harder to investigate. The name P7 comes from a prefix the attackers used in their programming code. While that detail won't mean much to most iPhone owners, the changes behind it are concerning. The spyware now performs more data collection directly on the infected phone and gives attackers additional control over what happens next. Apple told CyberGuy that DarkSword originated from sophisticated mercenary spyware developed at considerable expense. After the spyware leaked, the technology became available to common criminals. What can DarkSword spyware steal from your iPhone? Once attackers successfully compromise a vulnerable device, P7 DarkSword can reach information that most people would consider deeply private. Researchers identified several capabilities in the spyware's code. For someone who keeps sensitive documents or financial information on an iPhone, the potential exposure is serious. However, these findings describe the spyware's capabilities. They do not establish that attackers successfully stole every type of information from the device involved in the investigation. How P7 DarkSword communicates with hackers One particularly troubling feature is how frequently the spyware can contact its operators. According to iVerify, P7 DarkSword uses a command-and-control system that can check for instructions every 15 seconds. Attackers can change that interval remotely. This allows the spyware to receive new instructions after the initial infection. For example, an attacker could direct it to collect additional files or examine information stored on the device. The malware also supports commands that scan the phone's file system and execute JavaScript inside its running environment. Researchers found that the spyware injects its communication component into SpringBoard, a core iPhone system process responsible for the Home Screen and other interface functions. The attackers also removed some diagnostic logging and reduced certain activities that could reveal the infection during an investigation. These changes make the spyware harder for security researchers to examine. However, iVerify did not establish that the malware is completely undetectable. APPLE AIRDROP, ANDROID QUICK SHARE FLAWS PUT PHONES AT RISK How does DarkSword infect an iPhone? DarkSword is associated with an iOS exploit chain that attackers can use to compromise vulnerable devices through malicious web content. Security researchers have linked the P7 variant to distribution through malicious advertisements and compromised websites, sometimes called watering-hole attacks. That means someone using an outdated, vulnerable iPhone could encounter malicious content while browsing the web, potentially without realizing anything unusual happened. However, these attacks depend on exploitable security weaknesses. Installing Apple's security updates protects against the known vulnerabilities used by earlier DarkSword attacks. The original iVerify investigation focuses primarily on how P7 operates after infection. It does not fully reconstruct how the customer encountered the malicious content. That's why the exact circumstances of that particular infection remain unclear. Is your iPhone vulnerable to DarkSword spyware? Earlier DarkSword attacks targeted iPhones running iOS 18.4 through iOS 18.7. Apple told CyberGuy that it patched the underlying vulnerabilities in 2025, before DarkSword first leaked. The company also released a security update in March 2026 for older devices that could not install newer versions of iOS. According to Apple, iPhones running the latest available updates for iOS 15 through iOS 27 remain protected against the known DarkSword exploits. Researchers also identified exploit components associated with iOS 18.7 in the newer P7 investigation. However, they have not confirmed that the spyware can compromise fully updated iPhones. As of October 2026, iOS 27 is Apple's current major iPhone software generation. However, the latest available update depends on your iPhone model. Devices that have not received available security updates may remain exposed to known vulnerabilities. How to protect your iPhone from DarkSword spyware The research is a reminder that even sophisticated phone security can face serious threats. Fortunately, there are steps you can take to reduce your exposure. Start with these protections, especially if you've been putting off a software update. 1. Install the latest iPhone security updates Apple regularly releases updates that fix vulnerabilities attackers can exploit. Checking for updates is especially important if you haven't updated your iPhone recently. To check your current version and install updates: Next, go to Settings > General > Software Update > Automatic Updates and enable Automatically Install. This helps your phone receive future security fixes without relying on you to remember. 2. Enable Background Security Improvements On iOS 27, Apple also offers Background Security Improvements. These provide additional protections between major software updates. This setting adds another layer of protection against newly discovered security problems. 3. Be cautious with unfamiliar websites and use strong antivirus software Avoid opening unexpected links in text messages or emails, especially when they pressure you to act quickly. Malicious web content has played a role in previously documented iPhone attacks, so this is a sensible precaution. Consider using strong antivirus software that offers malicious website blocking, phishing protection and scam-link warnings. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at Cyberguy.com. These features can help you avoid dangerous content before you open it. However, iPhone security apps cannot perform the same deep malware scans available on computers. They also cannot guarantee detection or removal of sophisticated spyware like P7 DarkSword. That's why keeping iOS updated remains essential. HOW TO FIND COMPROMISED PASSWORDS ON IPHONE AND ANDROID 4. Consider Apple's Lockdown Mode If you believe someone may specifically target you with sophisticated spyware, Apple's Lockdown Mode offers stronger security protections. It restricts certain website technologies, messaging features and device connections to reduce opportunities for attackers. Apple designed this feature for people facing unusually advanced threats. Most iPhone owners won't need it because some everyday features become limited. According to Apple, security researchers confirmed that the known DarkSword exploits do not work on devices with Lockdown Mode enabled. To turn it on: For more on targeted attacks, read our article about Apple's spyware warnings reaching iPhone users in 110 countries. 5. Protect your passwords and financial accounts Because P7 DarkSword can target keychain and cryptocurrency wallet information, pay attention to unusual activity in your sensitive accounts. Apple recommends protecting your iPhone with a passcode, using a strong password and two-factor authentication (2FA) for your Apple Account and installing apps from the App Store. Use a reputable password manager to generate and securely store strong, unique passwords for every account. Review alerts from financial services. Keep in mind that a password manager cannot protect credentials if sophisticated spyware has already compromised your device. If you have credible evidence that your iPhone was compromised, change important passwords using another trusted device. Also, contact your financial institutions if you notice unauthorized transactions. Cryptocurrency users should seek trusted wallet-security assistance before moving funds. These steps can limit damage after an account compromise, although they cannot remove sophisticated spyware from an infected phone. 6. Know when to seek professional help Advanced spyware may operate without obvious symptoms. Your iPhone could appear to work normally, so a healthy battery or the absence of strange pop-ups cannot prove that your device is clean. If you receive what appears to be an Apple threat notification, verify it by signing in directly at account.apple.com, rather than clicking links in the message. Apple provides additional information about recognizing and responding to these alerts on its threat notification support page. Then seek assistance from a qualified mobile security specialist. A routine security app scan may not detect an advanced infection. What to do if you think your iPhone has already been infected If you have strong reason to suspect spyware, avoid using that phone for sensitive activities until you've received guidance. From a separate trusted device, secure important accounts and review recent sign-ins. You should also preserve any genuine Apple threat notifications or suspicious messages. For a potentially targeted attack, contact a specialist before erasing your iPhone. Resetting the device can destroy evidence investigators may need, and it may complicate efforts to determine what happened. Kurt's key takeaways What concerns me most about this discovery is how much information attackers could potentially collect from a single phone. We trust our iPhones with some of our most private information, often without thinking twice about where we store it. P7 DarkSword shows how dangerous that access could become if attackers successfully exploit a security weakness. It's also troubling to see expensive mercenary spyware leak into the hands of common criminals. Apple says the vulnerabilities behind these known attacks were patched before the spyware leaked, which is reassuring for people who keep their devices updated. I would check your iPhone's software version today, especially if you haven't updated it recently. And if you use your phone for financial transactions or store sensitive personal information, take a few minutes to review your account security. articles.title: Vibe coding is turning the music gear world upside down
articles.summary: LLMs have led to an explosion of custom firmware and hacks for synths, samplers, and grooveboxes.
articles.body: If you spend any time on r/synthesizers or watch a lot of synth videos on YouTube, you’ve probably noticed the explosion of custom firmware for hardware synthesizers, samplers, and grooveboxes. What unites almost all of them is that they were made possible by increasingly sophisticated vibe coding tools. These sorts of custom firmware were exceedingly rare in the pre-LLM days, and required both deep expertise and an incredible investment of time. It could take weeks or months to add a simple feature like velocity sensitivity to a Korg Volca. Now, hobbyist hackers are able to turn Temu synths into full-fledged grooveboxes in a matter of days. Elektron’s budget-friendly Model:Cycles, Digitone, Octatrack, and Digitakt have all gained new capabilities with Claude’s help. Roland’s SP-404 MKII, Ableton’s Push 3 and Move, Akai’s MPC Live and MPC One, as well as the vintage MPC 2000, Novation’s Circuit, Arturia’s MicroFreak, and even Zoom’s 14-year-old Multistomp pedal line have all seen new custom firmware released in the last month or so. Leading the charge is a tiny $70 Yamaha DX-7 clone: the M-Vave FM-1. It was already on its way to being the synth of the summer. The dirt-cheap price and faithful recreation of classic FM tones made it incredibly popular with first-time synth buyers, hobbyists, and synthfluencers alike. Inevitably, someone wondered how far they could push the hardware and, with the help of AI, kickstarted an arms race. The FM-1 now has dozens of custom firmwares available. Many of the most popular — Felucca, Sloop, and x0x — list Claude as a contributor on their GitHub page or include explicit disclosures about their use of AI. Baudgirl is also suspected to have been created with the assistance of AI, but the developer did not reply to a request for comment. [Media: What started as a surprisingly good, but basic DX-7 clone now supports a variety of synth engines, including virtual analog, sample playback, multi-track sequencing, and a variety of UI designs. It’s not terribly shocking that someone was willing to risk bricking a $70 Temu synth. Generally, the gear that has benefited from this surge of vibe-coded custom firmware is older or more affordable. Roman Rusinov, who posts on Reddit as themanro and releases music under Farlow, set his sights on the Zoom MS-70CDR. It’s a budget multi-effects pedal from 2012 that has a reputation for punching above its weight, making it a staple of affordable synth setups. He started by learning about ZDL, a project that reverse-engineered the Multistomp format, allowing for the creation of custom effects. He eventually coaxed the pedal into running NAM A2 Lite captures and custom impulse responses (IRs), turning it into a full-fledged modeler capable of emulating vintage amps. “I was already using AI for some work stuff and figured this would be a great case to try learning some vibe-coding fundamentals and get a project going,” he told The Verge. “There was a lot of trial and error of finding the limitations of the hardware and software.” He says he’s thrilled to be part of a broader movement. “Somehow it all lined up with all these other projects pushing the boundaries of older hardware and breathing new life into it. I love that,” he said. “If you own the hardware, you should be able to do whatever you want with it.” [Media: 18nelli, the developer behind Modded Cycles, was similarly motivated by a desire to revitalize some forgotten gear. “I had an Elektron Model:Cycles that left me feeling frustrated,” he told The Verge. He said that it felt designed “just to push us to buy their more expensive gear.” But recent AI advances made him believe he could add features to the groovebox, which hasn’t had an official update since May 2021. So he opened up his Cycles, documented all the parts, and started working with Claude Code to implement his first hack — six-track audio over USB. That has since exploded into a community project with multiple mods contributed by others, several standalone custom firmwares, and even the ability to turn your Model:Cycles into a Model:Samples. “I think not using LLMs would have been counterproductive,” he said. “I probably would have spent a massive amount of time and energy on just a single feature, whereas my real goal is to actually create and make music with amazing mods.” [Media: Modded Cycles has certainly been one of the more frantic projects out there. I recently watched as five firmware updates hit the announcements channel on its Discord in one day. 18nelli has since said he plans to pause adding new features and slow development to polish the existing code and stomp out some bugs. New mods and firmwares hit the web almost every day now. If there’s a favorite piece of gear in your arsenal that you wish had one killer feature, there’s a chance it might end up on a GitHub page sooner than later. Heck, if you just wish your pocket synth could play NES ROMs, that’s also a distinct possibility. Of course, there is some risk here. These firmwares are often less thoroughly tested than the manufacturer’s official one. The response to the modding scene has varied from company to company, with many choosing to remain silent. Elektron banned links to custom firmware from their forums. In a statement posted on its official forums, the company said, “We would always warn against modifications to our firmware and/or machines that could brick them … Something that looks like a simple change in isolation can lead to major problems elsewhere, particularly when a later official OS arrives, and can confuse users about which features are officially available on our machines.” Others, like M-Vave, seem to be embracing the movement. It recently announced FM1 Open, an open-source firmware with additional features, plus a development kit and a firmware-flashing tool for the community. The response to music gear that uses AI and vibe coding has been mixed. Devices like the Polyend Endless have sparked some ire. And music-making subreddits are awash in people complaining about vibe-coded plugin slop. But so far the community has been less hostile to vibe-coded firmware. Maybe, in part, because breathing new life into old instruments helps keep their Gear Acquisition Syndrome (GAS) in check.

articles.title: Narayani Shastri joins 'Mahadev & Sons' as Bhanu; says 'I’ve never been an actor who plays it safe'
articles.summary: The return of the formidable Bhanu to the world of ‘Mahadev & Sons’ is set to shake up relationships in the family.
articles.body: The return of the formidable Bhanu to the world of ‘Mahadev & Sons’ is set to shake up relationships in the family. Actress Narayani Shastri is stepping into the role of Bhanu. Known as a force to reckon with, Bhanu arrives with a chilling agenda - to destroy Rajji (Garvita Sadhwani) and Dheeraj’s (Aasim Khan) relationship and bring the Mahadev family to its knees.Bhanu will be seen making a dramatic entry during Dheeraj and Rajji’s wedding and will threaten Rajji with a evil promise to ruin her life and marriage. She will set the stage for a battle that could tear the family apart. Dheeraj and Rajji vow to protect their loved ones and keep their families united but Bhanu is determined to dismantle everything they hold dear. Bhanu’s plans are only becoming dangerous. When the Mahadev family decides to accompany the newlyweds on their honeymoon to Mumbai, their plans for a joyful getaway take an unexpected turn as they come face-to-face with Bhanu. The trip threatens to become a hotbed of confrontation, unsettling revelations and calculated moves. As she sets out to drive a wedge between the family members, Dheeraj and Rajji face the daunting challenge of keeping their loved ones together while Bhanu works relentlessly to pull them apart.Sharing her thoughts about joining the show Narayani Shastri says, “I’ve never been an actor who plays it safe. When I look at a script, I'm not captivated by a character who is perfectly good or cartoonishly evil. I look for the grey, the mess, the real human stuff. That’s exactly why joining Mahadev & Sons was an immediate yes for me. The show is already a massive hit, which is fantastic, and it is an honour to be trusted with disrupting its storyline. Here is a character who is a sharp chess master, ensuring she is ten steps ahead. To play someone like that, you can't judge them from the outside. As an actor, my first job is to find her 'why' and empathise with her. Bhanu believes she’s the hero of her own story righting a massive wrong. That absolute, unshakeable conviction is the emotional fodder I pull from every time the director calls action. I thank the audiences for showing so much excitement towards my entry on the show and hope to entertain them with everything I have.”Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: It’s hard to imagine wireless headphones ever getting lighter than these
articles.summary: The Porta wireless headphones from Japan’s Final use a single wire structure for an ultra light design that weighs just 40 grams.
articles.body: If you’re on the hunt for lightweight wireless headphones but wearing earbuds or clip-ons never feels comfortable or secure, a relatively obscure Japanese headphone maker could have the solution. Final’s new Porta headphones feature an on-ear design supported by a headband but with a structure made from a single piece of wire so they weigh just 40 grams. For comparison, Marshall’s recently-launched Milton A.N.C. are also designed to be smaller on-ear headphones but weigh 200 grams. The Final Porta are available for preorder now through the company’s online store for 12,800 yen (around $80) with black or orange ear pads and shipping expected to start on October 23rd. The company also has an Amazon shop for US-based customers, but the Porta aren’t listed there yet. [Image: The Porta come with either black or orange ear pads. Sporting a design that looks loosely inspired by the lightweight headphones Sony bundled with its Walkmans decades ago, the Porta’s functionality is unsurprisingly basic. A 57mAh battery charges over USB-C and provides up to eight hours of use while the Porta are wirelessly paired to a device using Bluetooth 5.4 and streaming audio over the SBC and AAC codecs. There’s no active noise cancelation which is not uncommon for on-ear headphones that don’t create a full seal, but with an IPX4 rating you should be able to use the Porta in the rain or while working up a sweat without worrying about them getting damaged by the moisture.

articles.title: How a controversial lift on 'Dancing With the Stars' and a reference to Will Smith's Oscars slap led to pro dancer Val Chmerkovskiy's suspension
articles.summary: The controversy began when judge Carrie Ann Inaba told Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson that their routine included a move that is not allowed in traditional...
articles.body:
It's been quite a week for Dancing With the Stars drama, both in and out of the ballroom, with a judge accusing a pair of contestants of utilizing an illegal move during their routine and a professional dancer criticizing the judge in a social media post that got him temporarily suspended from the show.

The controversy began during the Oct. 13 episode of the ABC reality dance competition, dubbed Super Bowl Night, when Harry Shum Jr. and his professional dance partner, Jenna Johnson, performed a samba to "Yeah!" by Usher ft. Lil Jon & Ludacris. At one point, some of the dance troupe members hoisted Shum into the air.

After the performance, judge Carrie Ann Inaba told Shum and Johnson that their routine included a "lift," which is not allowed in traditional samba.

When Johnson questioned the ruling, Inaba proceeded to read her the definition.

"'A lift is any movement during which one of the dancers has both feet off the floor at the same time with the assistance or support of their partner,'" Inaba said before adding: "Yeah, a lift."

Inaba still gave the pair an 8 out of 10, leading fans to question the point of the judge's terse commentary.

Johnson later explained that she thought the lift rule applied only to the principal performers, not to backup dancers.

"You know what, it's hard, because usually when someone's called out for a lift, it's when your partner lifts you," Johnson told Extra after the episode. "But I absolutely hear Carrie Ann. She's a judge for a reason. She's gonna do her job, I'm gonna do mine. I'm gonna take the feedback."

The following day, Valentin Chmerkovskiy, Johnson's husband and a professional dancer paired with Jenna Dewan, took to Instagram to express his displeasure with Inaba by referencing what Will Smith told Chris Rock before his infamous slap at the 2022 Oscars.

"You almost saw Fresh Prince enter the ballroom last night," Chmerkovskiy wrote, a nod to the sitcom character that propelled Smith's career.

On Saturday, BBC Studios, which produces Dancing With the Stars , announced it was suspending Chmerkovskiy for a week, saying in a statement that the "well-being of everyone who works on" the show "is non-negotiable."

"Val's social media post was inappropriate and does not reflect the values or standards expected of anyone connected with the show," the statement said. "As a result, he will not participate in next week's show."

According to the Hollywood Reporter , Alan Bersten — who was eliminated earlier this season after competing with Giada De Laurentiis — will replace Chmerkovskiy as Dewan's professional dance partner on the next episode, which airs Tuesday at 8 p.m. ET.

Chmerkovskiy subsequently apologized for the post that triggered his suspension — the first in Dancing With the Stars history.

"In a moment where my instinct was to defend my wife, I made a poor decision to reference a meme to 'keep my wife's name' out of the conversation, without stopping to think through what else that reference could imply, which was genuinely never my intention," he said in a statement posted to Instagram. "Carrie Ann certainly didn't deserve to get caught in the middle of my bad judgment, and I hate that she was."

He added: "The last thing I want is to become a distraction from an important week or from the incredible work my dance partner Jenna Dewan is putting in. Please send Carrie Ann, Jenna, and the whole DWTS family lots of love during Dedication Night. I'll be watching and cheering everyone on!"
